 RBC Amplify 2027 – Business Analyst    
 What is Amplify?  
 RBC Amplify is an intensive summer innovation program that will put your skills to the test while building a product that could disrupt our company and beyond. If you’re a bright mind with fresh ideas, top of your class, own the hackathon circuit and are passionate about innovation, we want you! 
 Please note the application deadline is Sunday, November 15th at 11:59pm EST 
 What is the opportunity?  
 As a Business Analyst you will collaborate, innovate, ideate and build in a flexible, start-up environment.  
You will be responsible for not only organizing and managing your team’s project, building a business case and a captivating pitch – but also stretching outside your role to take on design tasks and help your team in all stages of the product building process. 
 You will tackle real RBC business challenges as a member of a cross-functional team of specialists (think: business, data, and programming) by developing a product or solution that you pitch to stakeholders at the end of the summer. 
 Over the course of the program, you will have access to subject matter experts, coaches, mentors, as well as technical and professional training and resources to bring your idea to life. 
 What will you do?  Discover. Research. Build. Pitch. 
 Immerse yourself in a business challenge with an intense focus on collaboration to develop an innovative product. 
 You will be challenged to step outside your comfort zone, and use your teamwork, communication and problem-solving skills to help your team succeed in ambiguity.

 Design, troubleshoot and develop your product. 
 Work with subject matter experts, mentors, executive sponsors and stakeholders (technology and business) to build your solution. 
 Exposure to design thinking, agile development and other tools, technologies and methodologies. 
 Executive presentations, developing strategy and communications for your project.

 Must have  
 Must be currently enrolled in a post-secondary institution, graduating between August 2027 and June 2028 (College, Undergrad, Master's or PhD).  
 Ability to understand and communicate business values. 
 Excellent interpersonal and highly developed communication skills (verbal and written). 
 Excellent critical thinking, time management and leadership skills. 
 Creative and analytical thinker who is self-driven and capable of working in a fast-paced team environment. 
 Ability to challenge the status quo and think outside the box to develop solutions. 
 Excellent teamwork, collaboration and problem-solving skills. 
 Strong interest or some experience in design using Adobe Creative Suite and/or Figma. 
 Nice to have  
 Experience with hackathons or case competitions 
 Experience in stakeholder engagement and working with end users and clients to understand their needs. 
 Experience with business presentations. 
 Experience with user research, prototyping, wireframing, and/or experience mapping (creating journey maps, personas, and service blueprints). 
 Experience with project management tools (ex. Jira, Confluence)  
 Experience with Figma or Design Tools
 Solid understanding of financial business insights, FinTech industry, startup industry or other related insights. 
 Interest and understanding of up and coming technology and methodologies.  
 What’s in it for you?  
 We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual. 
 A unique summer experience with the chance to develop a career at RBC. 
 Team up with students from diverse backgrounds and build lasting professional relationships. 
 Engage with leaders who support your development through coaching and learning opportunities. 
 Be a part of a dynamic, collaborative, progressive and high-performing team. 
 Contribute to real projects that can make a difference and have a lasting impact at RBC. 
 Tons of opportunity to grow specific skills for your future. 
 An all-around fun, innovative, and comfortable work environment

 You will play a critical role in transforming traditional claims processes using AI and advanced analytics. Your primary responsibilities will include designing, implementing, and optimizing intelligent systems across claims intake, investigation, and adjudication workflows. Paramount Commerce processes $5B+ annually across Interac, EFT, and real-time rails. As our first dedicated Solutions Engineer reporting to the CRO, you will bridge the gap between our commercial teams, technical capabilities, and merchants.
 Initially, you will design the playbook—establishing discovery frameworks and standardizing how Sales qualifies merchant technical needs. Once established, you will lead pre- and post-sales solutioning on live calls, translate complex money movement into actionable workflows, and hand fully scoped architectures over to Onboarding for execution.
 Key Responsibilities
 Lead Live Solutioning (Pre- and Post-Sale): Join calls with Business Development and Account Management to architect solutions in real time. Clearly articulate why a solution works, challenge client assumptions constructively, and act as an interpreter for merchant-specific payments terminology.
 Build Discovery Frameworks: Define the questions and parameters the commercial team must use during discovery to identify merchant requirements early.
 Document Workflows & Secure Sign-Off: Map payment workflows and the flow of money movement (e.g., swimlane diagrams). Document the agreed-upon solution and secure formal merchant sign-off.
 Own Onboarding Handoffs: Deliver fully scoped use cases and technical context to the Onboarding team so they can focus strictly on tracking integration and implementation.
 Drive the Product Feedback Loop: Act as the merchant advocate internally. Identify recurring trends, gaps, and feature requests—especially in new verticals—and feed them directly to Product and Engineering.
 Relay Technical Requirements: Read, interpret, and explain API documentation and integration paths without needing to write code.
 What You Bring
 Payments Depth: Deep experience in Solutions Engineering, Technical Pre-Sales, or Solutions Consulting within payments or fintech. Strong familiarity with North American payment rails (Interac, EFT, A2A), settlement flows, and money movement.
 Workflow Mapping: Hands-on experience producing clear visual documentation (swimlane diagrams, integration flows) that both developers and business leaders can understand.
 Technical Literacy: Ability to read and navigate API documentation, webhooks, and technical architectures to problem-solve integrations with merchant engineers.
 Merchant-Facing Presence: Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate technical details into business value, push back when a requested setup won't work, and guide clients to better solutions.
 Builder Mindset: Proven ability to create repeatable processes from scratch rather than just following existing playbooks.
 Who This Role Is For
 This role is for someone who has spent years watching deals get complicated because nobody owned the solution narrative. You've seen the post-signature scramble when integration requirements weren't properly scoped, and the frustration when sales promises don't match technical reality.
 You should be comfortable being the person who says "that won't work the way you think it will" in a room full of people who want to hear the opposite. You should be equally comfortable proposing the alternative that actually will.
 If you've been looking for a role where you build something from the ground up, translate complex merchant needs into clear operational realities, and work on problems that matter in a payments company that processes real volume, this is it.

ABOUT THIS ROLE

As Ashby’s first Demo Engineer, you’ll own the systems that make our demo environments reliable, current, and tailored — the infrastructure the entire go-to-market team leans on to show Ashby at its best. Today, AEs and SEs maintain and configure their own demo accounts by hand. That doesn’t scale: reps lose selling time, demos drift out of date, and every new product release widens the gap between what Ashby can do and what we can actually show live. Your job is to close that gap.

This is a net-new role. Right now, the work is split between ad hoc effort and a new set of disposable demo templates the Internal Platform team is building. You’ll own the layer on top of that foundation — customizing and extending those templates, generating realistic demo data, tailoring environments for specific verticals and new markets, and making sure every feature is demoable before it ships. You’ll sit within Solutions Engineering, reporting to the Global Head of Solutions Engineering, and partner closely with Internal Platform and Product teams.

Your work will be split roughly 70/30: about 70% owning, customizing, and extending the demo template system and the data and content inside it, and about 30% running demo readiness as a program — release readiness, documentation, and enablement so the GTM team always has current, credible demos to work with.

The best person for this job is genuinely hands-on technical — working with internal tools and configuration files, using APIs, and general data preparation — who gets energy from building leverage for a whole team rather than fixing one demo at a time.




YOU COULD BE A GREAT FIT IF:

 - 🛠 You’re comfortable working in JSON, calling REST / developer APIs, using AI tools, and scripting to configure and customize environments.

 - 🏗 You’re a builder, not just an operator. You get energy from creating systems and tooling that make a whole team more effective over time.

 - 🎥 You care deeply about demo quality. You understand what makes a product demo land, and you’re thoughtful about data realism and the narrative a demo needs to support.

 - 🧠 You have strong product intuition and can learn a deeply configurable product quickly, understanding how the different pieces connect.

 - 🔁 You have an iterative mindset. You like testing what works, refining over time, and improving based on what you learn from the field.

 - 🧩 You’re a systems thinker who would rather standardize and automate than manually repeat the same setup.

 - ⚡ You’re comfortable with ambiguity and enjoy a 0→1 role where the infrastructure is still being built around you.

 - 🤝 You partner well cross-functionally — with Engineering and with GTM — and can translate their needs into reliable systems.

 - 💙 You have empathy for the go-to-market teams you support and the Talent Acquisition space they sell into.




BONUS POINTS FOR:

 - 📊 You’ve built demo environments, demo data, or sandbox/trial environments at a SaaS company before.

 - 🧰 You’ve written automation scripts or tooling to generate data or configure environments at scale.

 - 🎬 You’ve built and maintained a library of reusable, templated environments or assets that others relied on.

 - 🤝 You have experience with HR tech, ATS workflows, or recruiting operations.




EXAMPLES OF THINGS YOU’LL WORK ON:

 - 🧱 Own the scaled demo system — customize and extend the demo environment infrastructure to support the GTM team.

 - 🗂 Generate realistic demo data — standardize and automate how demo environments are populated to eliminate manual setup.

 - 🎯 Build vertical- and market-specific demos — create tailored content for target verticals and additional languages as we move upmarket and expand internationally.

 - 🚦 Own demo readiness for new releases — make sure every feature is correctly configured and demoable in demo environments before it ships to GA.

 - 🧪 Stand up trial and sandbox environments — create templated environments prospects can use to test Ashby during the sales cycle.

 - 📚 Document how it all works — maintain clear documentation so the GTM team knows when and how to use each demo environment.




WHY BECOME A DEMO ENGINEER AT ASHBY?

You’ll define a role that doesn’t exist yet. This is a net-new role designed around a real business need. You won’t inherit a mature playbook — you’ll build the infrastructure that lets the whole GTM team demo at a higher level.

Your work will compound. A great live demo helps one deal. A reliable, current, well-documented demo system improves every demo the entire go-to-market team runs. If you like creating leverage, this role has a lot of it.

The product gives you something real to work with. Ashby has strong product-market fit, and that matters here. You’re not manufacturing excitement around a weak product — you’re making it effortless to show something that already resonates when it’s shown well.

You’ll sit at the intersection of Engineering and GTM. This is a rare blend of technical building and understanding what the field actually needs. You’ll help translate our product releases into live deals — and connect the two.

The surface area keeps growing. As we ship new features and expand into new product areas, new verticals, and new geographies, demo needs compound with each release. There is a lot to build, and it only gets more interesting.




REASONS YOU SHOULDN’T APPLY:

 - If you want to be customer-facing or closing deals, this isn’t the right role — the impact here happens behind the scenes.

 - If you’re not genuinely hands-on technical — comfortable in JSON, APIs, and data — the core of this job will be frustrating.

 - If you need a fully built environment and a finished playbook, the ambiguity of a 0→1 role with infrastructure still being built will feel uncomfortable.

 - If continuously maintaining and updating environments as the product changes sounds tedious rather than satisfying, this won’t be a fit.

 - If you’d rather build production product features than internal tooling and demo systems, you’ll likely want a different engineering role.




INTERVIEW PROCESS

Our interview process is thorough — we want to make sure this role is the right fit for you and that you’re the right fit for Ashby. Details on the process for this role will be shared by your recruiter.




BENEFITS

 - You’ll get the time to do things the right way; we put a lot of emphasis on high quality work and avoid quick hacks as much as possible.

 - Sell a product that our customers are truly excited about.

 - Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive!

 - 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby — do it when you feel financially comfortable.

 - $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval.




ABOUT ASHBY

We’re building the next generation of recruiting software and we’re starting with a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run an efficient and data-driven hiring process.

We are well funded and backed by great investors, including Y Combinator, Elad Gil and Lachy Groom. We have thousands of amazing customers including Snowflake, OpenAI, Shopify, Ramp, Notion, and Zapier (and many others who we cannot name!).

We're in the talent acquisition software business. We run the end-to-end hiring process through our own platform, and ensure a level playing field for all candidates. Reaching out to hiring managers or recruiters directly won't improve your odds of success. Please focus your energy on the quality of your application.

We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities.

Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked. 
 That is the whole job.
 Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.
 So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.
 At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.
 You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.
 Here is what "end to end" actually means.
 You are the account manager. We do not have any.  You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.
 You own the whole funnel, not the campaign.  Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.
 You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it.  We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.
 You can live anywhere.  We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.
 If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.
 If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.
 What the job looks like 
 Own a set of DTC accounts  as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
 Own the client relationship.  There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
 Audit before you touch anything.  Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
 Run brand and non brand as different businesses.  Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
 Know what PMax is actually doing.  The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
 Keep Google's automation on a leash.  Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
 Own the feed.  Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
 Own the tracking.  GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
 Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it.  Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
 Build the things the account needs.  Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.
 You are a fit if 
 You have done this with real money.  Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
 You are fluent in the whole stack , not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
 You are AI native, and you build.  This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
 You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level.  You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
 You are skeptical of your own numbers.  You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
 You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls.  Where you live is up to you.
 Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.
 You are not a fit if 
 "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
 You want to be told what to do this week.
 You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
 You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.
 Why this role is exciting 
 This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.
 You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.
 You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.
 You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

 Score the clinical reasoning quality of benchmark items: vignette accuracy and completeness, whether the vignette gives the answer away, answer correctness and gradeability, and trap quality;

Aperçu du poste : 
 Nous recherchons un(e) spécialiste des pratiques de gestion de produit, doté(e) d’un esprit pratique, pour mettre en œuvre et opérationnaliser les pratiques, les processus et les outils permettant à la gestion de produit de fonctionner de manière cohérente et efficace à grande échelle.
 Votre rôle consistera à traduire l’orientation stratégique de la gestion de produit en méthodes de travail concrètes et reproductibles. Vous créerez les modèles, les flux de travail, les normes, les automatisations, les tableaux de bord, la documentation et les expériences d’accompagnement qui aideront les gestionnaires de produit à appliquer ces pratiques dans leur travail quotidien.
 Vous travaillerez en collaboration avec les équipes de gestion de produits, de marketing de produits, de R-D, des ventes et des opérations afin de traduire les modèles opérationnels convenus en solutions claires, simples, mesurables et adoptées. La réussite ne se mesure pas uniquement à la production de documentation sur les processus. Elle se définit par la facilitation de l’adoption des méthodes de travail souhaitées, la réduction des tâches manuelles évitables, l’amélioration de la qualité et de la circulation de l’information, ainsi que par le soutien apporté aux équipes pour qu’elles utilisent de manière cohérente les outils et les processus sélectionnés.
 Votre journée en un coup d'oeil : 
 Mettre en œuvre la feuille de route des pratiques de gestion de produit définie par la direction de la gestion de produit, en traduisant les priorités en outils concrets, en flux de travail, en modèles, en lignes directrices et en plans de déploiement.
 Établir et maintenir des normes pratiques pour les activités essentielles de gestion de produit, notamment la documentation des problèmes du marché, la collecte d’informations sur les clients et le marché, les données de PLM vers les ordres d’achat, la mise à jour de la feuille de route, la réception des demandes, le triage, l’établissement des priorités et les transferts interfonctionnels.
 Configurer et améliorer les systèmes qui soutiennent ces pratiques, notamment SharePoint, Confluence, Azure DevOps, CRM, Wrike, Microsoft 365, Power Automate, les tableaux de bord et les flux de travail assistés par l’IA.
 Créer des modèles réutilisables, des listes de vérification, des exemples, des guides pratiques et des conseils en libre-service qui aident les gestionnaires de produit à appliquer les méthodes convenues avec moins d’ambiguïté et sans avoir à tout réinventer.
 Établir des structures d’information claires et des sources de référence pour les actifs de produit réutilisables, les connaissances sur le marché et les produits, les feuilles de route, les personas, les « tâches à accomplir » (Jobs-to-be-Done), les capacités et la documentation relative aux pratiques.
 Collaborez avec les gestionnaires de produit, les gestionnaires de marketing de produit, les responsables de produit, les responsables de la R-D et les intervenants commerciaux pour tester les flux de travail, cerner les points de friction et peaufiner les détails de mise en œuvre sans remettre en question les décisions stratégiques déjà prises.
 Favorisez l’adoption grâce à l’intégration, aux heures de consultation, à une formation concise, à des exemples, à des notes de mise à jour et à des communications ciblées sur le changement.
 S’assurer que les outils et les automatisations respectent les attentes de l’entreprise en matière de traitement de l’information, d’accès, de qualité, de traçabilité et de responsabilité humaine.
 À quoi ressemble la réussite? : 
 Les gestionnaires de produit consacrent moins de temps à des tâches de coordination évitables, à la recherche d’information, à la refonte de modèles et à la mise à jour manuelle des statuts.
 Les pratiques convenues se traduisent par des solutions opérationnelles et sont appliquées de manière cohérente par toutes les équipes.
 L’information échangée entre les équipes Produit, R-D, Marketing produit et Ventes est plus complète, mieux structurée et plus facile à exploiter.
 Les référentiels, les flux de travail, les tableaux de bord et les automatisations ont des responsables clairement identifiés et restent à jour après le lancement.
 L’adoption et la santé des processus sont visibles grâce à un petit ensemble de mesures fiables, et les améliorations sont fondées sur des données probantes.
 Les parties prenantes perçoivent ces pratiques comme un outil utile plutôt que comme une bureaucratie supplémentaire.

 Communication écrite claire et capacité à produire des normes, des instructions, des exemples et du matériel de formation concis.

 Territory: Greater Toronto Area, Ottawa, Manitoba, Saskatchewan
 Confident Remodels partners with a leading national home improvement retailer and provides software and process management that enable retailers and contractors to offer installed home improvements to homeowners in a convenient, consistent, and affordable manner. 
 The Regional Manager's primary responsibility is to drive revenue growth in their assigned territory. Additionally, the Regional Manager is responsible for supporting multiple retail locations within that territory, ensuring compliance with all program requirements. The Regional Manager should accomplish this by focusing on recruiting and retaining qualified Providers and developing and maintaining strong relationships with those Providers.
 This position is highly visible within the company and will have frequent contact with Senior Management, including the CEO and CFO. Additionally, the Regional Manager will be required to partner with other departments such as Compliance, Licensing, Central Processing, Call Center and Customer Solutions.
 An ideal candidate for this role will be able to drive performance within their assigned territory in terms of budget and other key metrics, such as customer satisfaction scores, cycle times, close percentage and service issue rate. The candidate must be able to work independently in a remote environment.
 Essential Functions: 
 Monitor Provider coverage/capacity in assigned territory, identify any coverage needs
 Source and recruit providers with expertise in various home improvement areas and identify those who can meet compliance requirements and fit the overall strategy
 Manage the recruiting needs and transition approved providers to the Compliance team for onboarding and activation
 Support Compliance Specialists in vetting providers through the application and activation process
 Manage Provider performance by training, coaching, influencing, and holding Contractors of varying size and sophistication accountable to Confident Remodels processes and standards
 Review business metrics and reports to identify performance opportunities, partner with Manager, National Accounts as necessary to develop executable action plans and implement those plans
 Conduct Monthly Business Reviews with Providers, discussing best practices and opportunities for improvement
 Coordinate store visits to meet with lead generators and store management and to cultivate relationships
 Identify, document and share Best Practices in Lead Generation, Sales, Installation and Service
 Determine ways to refine processes to automate and/or make them more efficient, both internally and for our external partners
 Communicate and execute new initiatives, programs, and policies in the field. 
 Assist in the resolution of service issues
 Perform other duties as required
 Position Requirements: 
 Prolonged periods of work at a desk and on a computer
 Certain tasks may occasionally require handling or moving materials weighing up to 15 pounds (7 kg)
 Minimum Qualifications: 
 High School Diploma or equivalent
 3+ years of retail or related experience
 Strong business acumen with an eye for detail and a commitment to excellence
 Sound judgment and strong problem-solving ability
 Exceptional communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to present information in a clear and concise manner
 Ability to interact effectively with all levels of an organization, including executive and C-level
 Exceptional organization skills
 Ability to juggle multiple projects at a time, while maintaining efficiency and sharp attention to detail
 Self-motivated, independent, and able to thrive in a remote work environment
 Highly organized with excellent time management skills and a demonstrated ability to meet deadlines
 Computer literate, including proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and other computer software
 Ability to adapt to changing or multiple priorities
 Must reside within reasonable proximity to a major airport to support frequent and efficient business travel.
 Ability to travel at least 50% of the time
 Assets : 
 Bachelor's Degree in Business Management, Project Management, or related discipline. 
 Knowledge of the home improvement industry
 The Regional Manager position requires travel greater than 50% of the time. The Regional Manager may be asked to perform additional tasks that are not listed above. In addition, the list of primary responsibilities may change over time.

 Paid time off
 And more!

 À propos de Browns : 
 Fondée à Montréal en 1940, Chaussures Browns a été bâtie sur un principe : prioriser les clients. Inébranlable dans sa mission d'offrir une expérience de magasinage inoubliable, Browns demeure l'intersection où le luxe rencontre l'abordabilité, et où chaque client est entendu. 
 Après des débuts modestes en tant que magasin familial, Browns est devenu le principal détaillant indépendant de chaussures en Amérique du Nord, avec plus de 70 magasins dans tout le Canada. Aujourd'hui, nous sommes fiers d'offrir une sélection de premier ordre de styles tendance et de collections exclusives qui incitent nos clients à revenir. 
 À propos du rôle: 
 En tant que rédacteur ou rédactrice, vous contribuerez à façonner la voix de Browns et à la faire rayonner partout où la marque s'exprime : campagnes promotionnelle, contenu éditorial, réseaux sociaux, site Web, courriels, boutiques et médias payants. Vous rédigerez le contenu qui bâtit l'identité de la marque tout en sachant décliner cette même idée tout au long de l'entonnoir de conversion pour créer des textes percutants qui respectent l'ADN de Browns. Au sein du Studio créatif, vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes du design, de la communauté et de l'éditorial, ainsi qu'avec celles de la performance et du CRM. 
 Principales responsabilités: 
 Façonner la voix de la marque 
 Participer à la définition et à l'évolution de la voix de Browns au fil de la croissance de la marque, et la traduire en lignes directrices claires et applicables par toutes les équipes. 
 Rédiger des concepts de campagne, des titres percutants, des manifestes et des slogans qui renforcent l'image de marque, en collaborant avec la direction artistique dès l'idéation. 
 Assurer la cohérence de chaque mot sur l'ensemble des points de contact, du slogan de campagne jusqu'au guide des tailles. 
 Adopter une perspective éditoriale 
 Rédiger du contenu éditorial avec un regard de curateur : récits de tendances, portraits de marques, sélections de produits et guides d'inspiration. 
 Collaborer avec l'équipe Communauté et éditorial pour rédiger des légendes, des scripts et des textes à l'écran conçus pour capter l'attention lors de la navigation et de la recherche. 
 Décliner le message tout au long de l'entonnoir de conversion 
 Traduire les concepts de marque en textes axés sur la performance : publicités sur les réseaux sociaux, référencement payant (SEM), bannières Web, objets de courriel et pages d'atterrissage. 
 Rédiger différentes variantes pour les tests A/B, analyser les résultats avec les équipes Performance et CRM, et réintégrer les apprentissages dans le développement de la marque. 
 Rédiger des fiches produits et des textes pour le site qui soient clairs, utiles et fidèles à la personnalité de Browns. 
 À l'échelle de l'entreprise 
 Rédiger pour les boutiques : vitrines, signalétique, matériel de point de vente et événements en magasin. 
 Collaborer avec nos partenaires de traduction pour s'assurer que le français et l'anglais véhiculent la même idée et le même ton, et non seulement une traduction mot à mot. 
 Utiliser judicieusement les outils d'IA pour élaborer des variantes et des premiers jets, conformément aux normes créatives de Browns, tout en préservant une voix authentique et humaine. 
 Votre Première Année : 
 Une voix Browns harmonieuse et reconnaissable à travers les campagnes, les fils d'actualité, le site Web et les boutiques. 
 Des lignes directrices rédactionnelles concrètes et réellement adoptées par l'ensemble de l'entreprise. 
 Des textes de performance qui obtiennent d'excellents résultats aux tests tout en restant fidèles à l'identité de marque. 
 Du contenu éditorial qui donne envie au public de lire Browns, et pas seulement d'y magasiner.

 3 à 5 ans d'expérience à titre de rédacteur ou rédactrice pour une marque de mode, de commerce de détail, de beauté ou d'art de vivre, en agence ou au sein d'une publication. 
 Un portfolio polyvalent démontrant votre savoir-faire : campagnes de marque, contenu éditorial et textes axés sur la conversion. 
 Un sens inné de l'éditorial : vous savez raconter une histoire captivante, pas seulement aligner des phrases.

 Town Web · HeyGov · ClerkMinutes. Remote, Central US hours.
 Here's a video to tell you more about this role! 
 About us 
 We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government customers in almost every state in the U.S.
 Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.
 The role 
 Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that  only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.
 This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.
 It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem occurring on the events calendar on the client’s homepage, or is happening within the calendar of events widget that is embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name showing up only in the transcript or is it showing up in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.
 What you will do 
 Delight clients 
 Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
 Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
 Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
 Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates
 Own the problem from start to finish 
 Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
 Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
 Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue
 Diagnose, then escalate 
 Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
 Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
 Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
 Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review
 Knowledge base and AI support 
 Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
 Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume
 Write troubleshooting guides that separate look-alike problems, so the next person, or Fin, can tell them apart
 Tune Fin: review where it failed, fix the article, and teach it to ask a clarifying question when a request could mean two things
 Record short training videos so clients can learn at their own pace
 Support and onboarding 
 Handle the conversations Fin cannot resolve across Town Web (websites), HeyGov (forms, payments, reservations, campaigns), and ClerkMinutes (agendas, transcripts, minutes)
 Help new clients through onboarding with the projects team so they reach value quickly
 Get on a call when a situation needs a human voice
 Account care 
 Build real relationships with your assigned accounts
 Understand what each client is trying to accomplish, what they use, what they do not know we offer, and where they will need help before they ask
 Run proactive, recurring check-ins instead of waiting for tickets. For example, reach out a few weeks after go-live to review how their forms are performing
 Use product usage data to spot clients who are not getting full value yet
 Spot opportunity 
 Tell clients about services they do not use yet (digital forms, payments, .gov domains, accessibility, training) without it feeling like a pitch
 Flag possible expansion and renewal opportunities to the sales team
 Training 
 Get clients to real proficiency with the product, not just past their immediate question
 Work with Product Managers to co-host webinars about new features, or training.
 Tools you will use : Intercom and Fin, Linear, Claude, our help center, screen recording, Zoom phone.
 How we work 
 Delight over deflection. The goal is happy, successful clients, not fewer conversations
 Ownership over routing. A hard case is yours until it is resolved
 Diagnose before you escalate. A developer should never have to ask what the client actually saw
 Documentation is the foundation everything else runs on, not an afterthought
 Teaching over ticket-closing. Proficiency, not just an answer
 Who you are 
 You have done support somewhere known for it. The standard we have in mind is Basecamp: competent, calm, and trusted to make the call
 Hospitable by nature. You make people feel comfortable and cared for. A background in hospitality or another service-first field is a plus
 Technically curious. You read the error, open the browser console, follow the trail into the code with Claude's help, and you are not afraid to look
 At home with developers. You know what a good bug report contains and you have filed plenty
 High autonomy. You decide, act, and report. You do not wait to be told
 A clear, warm, precise writer, with clients and across teams
 A natural teacher, patient with less technical users
 Able to see the whole account, not just the ticket in front of you
 Experience 
 SaaS support or client success in a role where you worked directly with engineers
 An issue tracker used daily: Linear preferred, Jira or similar is fine
 Intercom or similar support tooling. Experience with an AI support agent is a plus
 Writing or maintaining a knowledge base
 Nice to have: government or municipal software, WordPress-based websites, AI coding assistants
 Work style 
 Independent and ownership-driven. You do not need heavy oversight to perform
 Comfortable wearing several hats across products and brands
 Comfortable in a lean, documentation-first team
 Proactive rather than reactive with accounts
 What success looks like 
 Clients describe working with us as a great experience
 No client has to ask who is handling their problem. They already know it is you
 Issues you file get fixed without a developer asking for more detail
 Tickets stop recurring, not just get answered
 Help center articles created or improved every week, and Fin resolving more each month
 Repeat questions turned into product fixes or automation
 Expansion and renewals tied to the accounts you touch
 Account relationships that are trusted, not just responsive
 Location and hours 
 Remote, working Central US hours.
 Benefits 
 Internet stipend
 Gym membership or wellness stipend
 Public holidays for your country of residence, plus 20 paid vacation days

 Apply through Workable and answer the question via loom video: "Tell us about a time you went above and beyond for a client or your last company." Be specific
 Complete the Culture Index survey. We do not process applications without it

 Job Overview 
 We seek a Principal Network Engineer to serve as the technical lead for our enterprise network transformation. This is the highest-level individual contributor role on the Network Engineering team. You will design the Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) framework, manage our Palo Alto Panorama environment, and make key decisions where complexity and security meet. You will work closely with the Senior Manager of Network & Cloud Infrastructure and partner with Identity and Access Management (IAM), Cloud Infrastructure, and Security teams. Together, you will build a network that verifies identity, checks device posture, and enforces least privilege from edge to cloud, helping our teams around the world create and collaborate securely. You will bring this project to a definitive close.
 Location and Work Arrangement 
 This role is based at our Montreal, Quebec, Canada office and follows a hybrid schedule designed to support in-person collaboration. Employees are expected to work onsite on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, with the flexibility to work remotely or onsite on Mondays and Fridays.
 What You'll Do 
 Act as the technical expert for the Network 2.0 ZTNA program — own the architecture, lead build reviews, establish engineering standards, and address any critical issues during implementation.
 Build and validate the full ZTNA architecture across all primary and international sites — defining network zones, segmentation policy, and device posture requirements that eliminate lateral movement risk.
 Manage Palo Alto Panorama at the platform level — template hierarchy, device group creation, policy distribution oversight, and configuration drift prevention across all on-premises and cloud-connected Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs).
 Develop the AWS and Palo Alto Panorama cloud integration — detailing how cloud-native firewall policy, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) topology, and on-premises ZTNA fabric combine within a unified enforcement plane.
 Lead the Palo Alto Cloud Identity Engine (CIE) architecture in Year 2, jointly with IAM — build the identity-to-network enforcement model, define the network zone taxonomy, and direct the migration from IP-based user firewall rules to identity-based rules.
 Direct GlobalProtect architecture decisions — agent configuration, split tunneling policy, certificate trust chain, and version compliance standards upheld through Intune.
 Develop and keep current the network architecture documents, decision records, and runbook library that the broader team relies on to carry out tasks. You establish the standard; the team adheres to it.
 Lead the global site topology mapping effort by detailing all international sites. Define the tiered support model and produce the hardware refresh sequencing plan linked to the ZTNA rollout waves.
 Partner with the Automation / Network Reliability Engineer to build self-healing policy frameworks, Panorama API automation patterns, and Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) pipeline standards for network configuration changes.
 Represent Network Engineering in cross-functional architecture reviews alongside IAM, Cloud Infrastructure, Security, and Central Technology — you bring the network angle in conversations where enterprise architecture is decided.
 What You'll Bring 
 10+ years of enterprise network engineering with demonstrated depth in large-scale architecture building — not just operations.
 Advanced knowledge of Palo Alto NGFW and Panorama — template hierarchy, device groups, security policy development, Network Address Translation (NAT), decryption policy, and multi-virtual-system (vsys) environments.
 Proven ZTNA architecture experience — you have built a ZTNA deployment, not just configured one; you understand the segmentation model, the policy logic, and the failure modes.
 Comprehensive knowledge of GlobalProtect — covering agent architecture, gateway configuration, certificate trust, split tunneling policy, and troubleshooting issues across diverse endpoint types on a large scale.
 AWS network architecture hands-on — VPC build, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, AWS Network Firewall, and cloud-native connectivity patterns that integrate with on-premises enforcement.
 Understanding of identity-to-network enforcement patterns — how identity signals (Okta groups, Entra device compliance, CIE) translate into firewall policy and how that architecture scales.
 Grasp of Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) concepts and Prisma SD-WAN or equivalent — intelligent path selection, application-aware routing, and WAN optimization in a multi-site enterprise.
 Experience authoring network architecture documentation, design decision records, and engineering standards that other engineers can build against with confidence.
 Ability to work independently as a trusted technical partner to a senior manager — you provide the technical depth so the manager can focus on the program, and you keep work moving without close supervision.
 Clear communicator across technical and non-technical audiences. You can explain a zone segmentation model to a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and a Panorama template hierarchy to a junior engineer in the same afternoon.
 Professional proficiency in French and English is required for this role. English is necessary to communicate and collaborate regularly with colleagues and leaders based in the United States who primarily work in English.
 What Sets You Apart 
 Hands-on experience with Palo Alto Cloud Identity Engine (CIE) — integrating Okta or Entra group membership into NGFW policy enforcement.
 Network automation depth — Python, Ansible, or Panorama API scripting for policy automation, compliance checking, or self-healing configurations.
 Experience in GCP network configuration — VPC Service Controls, Cloud Armor, or hybrid connectivity models connecting GCP and on-premises ZTNA fabric.
 Experience working in a multi-studio, multi-site entertainment or gaming enterprise with geographically distributed international infrastructure.
 Active certifications: PCNSE (Palo Alto Certified Network Security Engineer), ZTNA specialist, or AWS Advanced Networking Specialty.

 Make our brands the most loved and trusted pet brands in North America, not just the most bought.  We're a profitable DTC pet brand selling premium stainless steel cat water fountains, filters and accessories.  Better Everyday : review every brand moment against its goal, and make the next one bigger, cheaper or better.
 Speed Is King : jump on cultural moments and press opportunities the same day, and launch every brand moment on schedule.
 Work Smart : use partners, agencies and AI instead of a large team. For example, use Claude to draft press pitches and partner outreach, track media mentions, turn reviews into customer stories, and build the monthly brand-health report from search, survey and press data.
 Overdeliver : bring the CEO new partnership and brand-moment ideas before being asked, and get more press and goodwill from each moment than the plan called for.

 More people know and search for our brands : branded search volume and direct traffic, monthly vs the same month last year

elia est une plateforme SaaS B2B de gestion de l'espace de travail qui aide les entreprises à réinventer leur environnement de travail : réservation de bureaux et de salles, gestion des visiteurs, capteurs IoT et occupation, gestion d'actifs, affichage numérique, casiers intelligents, et plus encore. Nos clients incluent de grandes organisations à travers le Canada, les États-Unis et quelques autres pays.
Nous sommes une équipe technique, en pleine croissance, où chaque personne a un impact direct sur le produit et où l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de construire.

Nous cherchons une développeur·euse full stack pour rejoindre notre équipe de développement et faire évoluer lʼensemble de la plateforme elia. Vous ferez partie d'une cellule compacte de 4 développeurs, 1 Product Owner et 1 Product Designer, et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec le CTO et le reste de l'équipe pour livrer le code de qualité, déployé en production à tous les jours.
On cherche quelqu'un qui fait avancer l'équipe : qui pose les bonnes questions, qui n'a pas peur de challenger nos décisions (ni de se faire challenger), qui veut continuellement apprendre et sʼaméliorer.

Participer activement aux décisions sur les fonctionnalités à développer et lʼarchitecture à mettre en place pour y arriver.
Développer de nouvelles fonctionnalités dans la plateforme elia, du front-end au back-end, en assurant la qualité et la pérennité du code.
Effectuer les revues de code.
Déployer l'application en production, la surveiller, la maintenir et régler les incidents
Proposer des solutions d'amélioration continue pour l'efficacité de l'équipe et l'expérience développeur.
Prendre partie aux décisions sur les processus à intégrer et aider à les mettre en place.
 
Profil recherché
Minimum 3 ans d'expérience en développement dʼapplication web
BAC en génie logiciel ou informatique ou formation en développement web (AEC, DEC)
Excellentes connaissances de React, TypeScript, Kotlin/Java
Bonnes connaissances de SQL (PostgreSQL), CSS (Tailwind)
Avoir à cœur la qualité du code et les bonnes pratiques de développement (SOLID, TDD, etc.)
Être capable de travailler dans un environnement Cloud avec AWS
Curiosité technique, toujours vouloir en apprendre plus, à sʼaméliorer
Capacité à synthétiser de l'information complexe et à la vulgariser

Chez Elia, l'IA fait partie intégrante de notre façon de travailler. On ne cherche pas à vous convaincre que l'IA accélère le développement. En partie du principe que vous le savez déjà. Ce qu'on recherche :
Vous utilisez déjà Claude (ou un outil équivalent) au quotidien, pas seulement pour écrire du code, mais pour repenser votre façon de travailler ;
Vous êtes capable de nous montrer une façon différente de faire les choses, pas seulement de suivre le mouvement ;
